searchText: I recall hearing that we're using `engine_exchangeTransitionConfigurationV1` as a "ping" to ensure users have their EL/CL connected. This seems reasonable to me, I'm wondering if there are any docs about when we should ping? I assume we ping at startup but I'm wondering if ELs expect regular pings? From my discussions with <@!758579010027782144> , we can ping whenever we like, ELs haven't put any constraints but I guess whenever there is a change (or new entry) detected for TTD or terminal block hash or its number, we *should* run this config match once the *dust settles* on the merge/terminal config (merge justified), it could be some timer event for http, for websockets it could just be post connection thats my current understanding 🙂 I'd ping on a regular pace, something like 60 seconds. This looks like a simple approach and shouldn't create an overhead I recall <@!291925846556540928> saying that we’ll get noise in the EL logs if we don’t ping. Perhaps I got my wires crossed. Not sure about this. Why do we get noise if we *don't* ping? I assumed it was some mechanism to ensure that the EL has a CL connected when the time comes. I think no. The noise should happen if exchange ended up in mismatch in configuration params between layers Kintsugi testnet will be with `klin` meta spec? Or other superseeding testnet published? there will be a long-lived testnet akin to `kintsugi` but using the `kiln` metaspec. it is not published yet. it's what `devnet-4` is part of building towards Thank you <@!654267572107083777> So in case of attaching Kintsugi with Klin spec, existing config can be used? https://github.com/eth-clients/merge-testnets.git No there would be new configs released soon. However nothing changes in the format of the configs, just the values will be updated. Thank you! I would expect a merge ready EL to surface warnings that it's not getting pinged I suspect this is the most valuable use of this method As it is likely clients are released with correct configs But highly likely users manage to not get them talking correctly then we probably need to set some kind of QoS for this request. Like CL should call this method at least once in a minute Right, fair Iiuc that is what infura was thinking but maybe I'm wrong <dannyryan> Or at least that clients log when they receive pings and an absence of such logs is a warning to the user ELs are not necessarily my domain, but I think the ping idea has merit. Specifically, emitting a sad log when there’s been no ping for N seconds. The spec could declare that a CL SHOULD ping on 60s interval and that an EL SHOULD alert the user if it doesn’t receive a ping after 120s. Sending *anything* to the auth port might also be enough to reset the EL warn timer. On a separate topic, I wanted to confirm that CLs are unaware of `TERMINAL_BLOCK_NUMBER`? I see it's a value in `TransitionConfigurationV1` but we're not supposed to be concerned if the `terminalBlockNumber` values mismatch. I've made a PR here to get the conversation started: https://github.com/ethereum/execution-apis/pull/189

excerpts.content: From my discussions with <@!758579010027782144> , we can ping whenever we like, ELs haven't put any constraints

excerpts.author: g11tech
excerpts.content: but I guess whenever there is a change (or new entry) detected for TTD or terminal block hash or its number, we *should* run this config match

excerpts.author: g11tech

excerpts.author: paulhauner
excerpts.content:
ELs are not necessarily my domain, but I think the ping idea has merit. Specifically, emitting a sad log when there’s been no ping for N seconds.

The spec could declare that a CL SHOULD ping on 60s interval and that an EL SHOULD alert the user if it doesn’t receive  a ping after 120s.

Sending *anything* to the auth port might also be enough to reset the EL warn timer.

excerpts.author: paulhauner
excerpts.content: On a separate topic, I wanted to confirm that CLs are unaware of `TERMINAL_BLOCK_NUMBER`? I see it's a value in `TransitionConfigurationV1` but we're not supposed to be concerned if the `terminalBlockNumber` values mismatch.
